explanation: Recursively extend a valid prefix. Add an opening parenthesis while opens remain, and a closing parenthesis only when more closes than opens remain. Each branch owns its extended prefix string.
timeComplexity: O(n·Cₙ), where Cₙ is the nth Catalan number Each of Cₙ leaves materializes 2n characters, and valid-prefix traversal contributes the same output-sensitive bound.
spaceComplexity: O(n²) auxiliary characters across up to 2n live prefix strings, plus O(n·Cₙ) output; Cₙ is the nth Catalan number. Prefix copying, unlike a shared buffer, retains strings of several lengths. The shared buffer and recursive depth are linear; immutable-prefix variants retain the separately stated prefix storage.
attribution: Unmodified reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/enumerate_balanced_parentheses.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Every generated prefix has at least as many opens as closes and never uses more than n opens. Completed prefixes are therefore balanced. Conversely, every balanced string follows exactly one sequence of these allowed opening/closing choices, so none are omitted or duplicated.
walkthrough: With two pairs, opening twice first gives (()); closing after the first open gives ()(). These are the two possible balanced strings.
edgeCases: Zero pairs produces one empty string.
A closing parenthesis cannot precede its matching opening.
Output ordering is not part of the contract.
